name: A0_net_loss
description: Anchor: any net loss (margin interest included) arms; 3% discount off the loss exit; frozen-high 95% reset. Identical to REF_lower3 / lower-price-reentry B_lower_3pct.
hypothesis: Reproduces the existing 3% strategy trade for trade (calibration anchor). Its trigger fires on financing-only losses (net loss with exit >= entry), which arm restrictions after sessions where price did NOT fall — e.g. the VGT 2023-01-03 -$143 exit that blocked a +$28k baseline winner. Counting those episodes per dataset quantifies the false-trigger problem the rest of the family tries to fix.

name: A1_price_loss_only
description: Arms only when exit_price < entry_price (pure price loss); financing-only losses never restrict. Discount/reset as A0.
hypothesis: Financing-only losses occur when price went sideways or up during the hold — not cascade conditions — so dropping them should recover blocked recovery winners (VGT 2023-01 type) at little or no bear-market cost: in 2000-02 cascades nearly every loss is a price loss, so A1 should keep A0's bear-market protection almost unchanged.

name: A2_material_05
description: Arms only when price return <= -0.5%. Discount/reset as A0.
hypothesis: A small materiality floor removes financing-only and hairline price losses (round-trip noise) while still restricting after every real decline; should behave like A1 with slightly fewer armings and no loss of 2000-02 protection.

name: A2_material_1
description: Arms only when price return <= -1%. Discount/reset as A0.
hypothesis: Same mechanism as A2_material_05 with a wider exemption band. The risk grows with the threshold: losses the floor exempts can repeat unrestricted in grinding bears. At -1% the exempted trades should still be few and small.

name: A2_material_2
description: Arms only when price return <= -2%. Discount/reset as A0.
hypothesis: At -2% the exemption starts to admit repeated moderate losses (a -1.5% loss can recur back-to-back in 2000-02); expect visible bear-window degradation vs A0/A1 in exchange for fewer blocked recoveries.

name: A2_material_3
description: Arms only when price return <= -3%. Discount/reset as A0.
hypothesis: The widest floor. Many 15-day loss exits in cascades lose 1-3% of price, so A3% should measurably re-open the 2000-02 repeated-loss problem; if it does NOT, the restriction's bear-market value comes from the few deep losses only.

name: A3_bands_a
description: Dollar-loss bands on |net P&L|: < $500 no restriction; $500-$5,000 arms with 3% discount; > $5,000 arms with 5% discount. Reset as A0.
hypothesis: Graduated severity: small losses (the -$143 type) free, moderate losses get the verified 3%, big losses demand 5%. Should keep most bear protection while freeing noise episodes; the 5% band risks V-bottom misses exactly where lower-price-reentry C (-5%) missed (2020-03, 2009 QQQ was fine for C).

name: A3_bands_b
description: Single dollar band: net loss < $1,000 in magnitude: no restriction; otherwise arms with the fixed 3% discount. Reset as A0.
hypothesis: The simplest materiality rule in dollars. A $1,000 floor on a $100k position is roughly a -1% net return floor, so it should behave like A2_material_1 but also exempt financing-heavy small losses; one parameter, easy to reason about.

name: A4_proportional_05
description: Severity-scaled: arms on any price loss; required decline = clip(0.5 * |price return|, 1%, 8%) off the loss exit. Reset as A0.
hypothesis: Proportional severity: tiny price losses impose only a 1% hurdle (nearly free re-entry, so V-bottom recoveries after small losses survive), deep losses demand more. With k=0.5 a -6% loss asks 3%: gentler than A0 almost everywhere; should dominate binary triggers IF severity, not existence, of the loss is what matters.

name: A4_proportional_10
description: Severity-scaled: arms on any price loss; required decline = clip(1.0 * |price return|, 1%, 8%) off the loss exit. Reset as A0.
hypothesis: k=1: the market must fall again by as much as it already cost us. In cascades this ratchets toward the 8% cap and should approach lower-price-reentry D's behaviour (strong 2000-02 protection, missed 2009/2026 rebounds); after small losses it stays near 1% and keeps recoveries. Tests whether one adaptive rule can span the B-vs-D regime split identified in the prior report.
